Sandbox_WaterPipes_RealisticPurification: When on, taps no longer purify tainted water automatically: tainted water stays tainted until you run it through a purifier tile. On by default as the survival baseline; turn it off to have taps serve clean water like vanilla.
Sandbox_WaterPipes_GeneratorRefuelThresh: A plumbed generator pulls fuel from the network once its tank drops below this percentage of its capacity. Set to 0 to disable auto-refuelling.
Sandbox_WaterPipes_GeneratorRefuelTarget: When auto-refuelling, the generator is topped up to this percentage of its tank (100 = full).
Sandbox_WaterPipes_PurifierFilterWear_to: How fast the electric purifier's filter wears out with use, as a percentage of the default rate. 100 = default (a full filter cleans about 5000 units of tainted water before it needs repair). 200 = wears twice as fast, 50 = half as fast. Set to 0 so filters never wear out and never need repairing.
Sandbox_WaterPipes_PressureModel_tooltip: How water pressure is worked out. Pressure is measured in metres of water column: height above a tap adds pressure, distance along the pipes spends it, and pumps create it. Realistic uses the full model. Simple counts height only, so distance never costs anything. Off restores the old behaviour, where water simply flows downhill however far it has to travel.
Sandbox_WaterPipes_PressurePerLevel: Pressure gained per floor of height (tenths)
Sandbox_WaterPipes_PressurePerLevel_tool: Pressure a source gains for each floor it sits above what it feeds, in tenths of a metre of water column. 30 = 3.0 per floor, which matches a real storey height. Higher values make rooftop tanks and water towers stronger.
Sandbox_WaterPipes_PressureContainerBase: Pressure a barrel or collector provides on its own floor, in tenths of a metre of water column, from the weight of its own water. 10 = 1.0, which lets a tap draw from about 20 tiles away on the flat. Raise this if taps in your base sit a long way from their barrels.
Sandbox_WaterPipes_PressureFrictionScale: How much pressure each pipe tile costs, as a percentage of the default. 100 = default. 200 = pipes lose pressure twice as fast, halving how far water travels. Set to 0 so distance never costs pressure and only height and pumps matter.
Sandbox_WaterPipes_HydraulicDemandScale_: How much a pipe is charged for the water its NEIGHBOURS are drawing. 100 = full realism: thirty sprinklers on one line starve each other, and only the ones nearest the pump run. 0 = the pre-4.x behaviour, where every consumer priced its run as if it were alone on the network, so any number of sprinklers ran off a single pump. Lower it if an existing farm stopped working and you would rather not rebuild it into zones.
Sandbox_WaterPipes_PumpHead_tooltip: Pressure a powered pump adds to its part of the network, in tenths of a metre of water column. 250 = 25.0, which matches a domestic pressure set. Pumps chained together add up. A sprinkler needs 20.0, so one pump runs sprinklers about 30 tiles away.
Sandbox_WaterPipes_PumpSuctionLimit_tool: How far below itself a pump can still lift water, in tenths of a metre of water column. 70 = 7.0, about two floors, which is the real limit for a surface pump because atmospheric pressure caps suction. A source further down will not prime, no matter how strong the pump is. Raise this if you want pumps to reach deep basements.
Sandbox_WaterPipes_PumpIntakeRate_toolti: How much water a pump draws from a well or open water each in-game minute. 20 = about 1200 litres an hour, which is on the modest side for a real pump. This is the main brake on infinite river water, so lower it if water feels too easy.
Sandbox_WaterPipes_PumpFromWaterBodies: Pumps can draw from rivers and lakes
Sandbox_WaterPipes_PumpFromWaterBodies_t: When on, a pump placed beside open water draws unlimited dirty water from it, which you can then clean with a purifier. Turn this off to keep water scarce: pumps will still work from wells and from your own barrels.
Sandbox_WaterPipes_DripBurstPressure: Pressure that bursts a drip emitter (tenths)
Sandbox_WaterPipes_DripBurstPressure_too: Above this pressure a drip emitter blows out and stops watering until you repair it, just like a real one. In tenths of a metre of water column: 150 = 15.0, well under a pump's 25.0, so a pump on the same line will burst your emitters unless you put a router in between and set a limit. Set to 0 so emitters never burst.
Sandbox_WaterPipes_SprinklerNoise_toolti: When on, a running sprinkler attracts zombies, which is the price you pay for watering a whole area at once. Turn it off if you would rather irrigate quietly.
Sandbox_WaterPipes_MainsSupply_tooltip: While the water service is still running, a plumbed sink or shower feeds your pipes instead of just drawing from them: it fills your containers and holds the network at mains pressure, so sprinklers run without a pump until the day the water is cut. Turn this off to keep the old behaviour, where plumbing a fixture switched its town water off and gave nothing back.
Sandbox_WaterPipes_MainsHead_tooltip: Pressure the town supply holds the network at, in tenths of a metre of water column. 250 = 25.0, the low end of what a real municipal main runs. A sprinkler needs 20.0, so at the default the mains runs sprinklers on its own. Lower it if you want pumps to still matter before the shutoff.
Sandbox_WaterPipes_MainsIntakeRate: Town water intake rate (litres per minute)
Sandbox_WaterPipes_MainsIntakeRate_toolt: How much water the town supply pushes into your network each in-game minute. 60 = 3600 litres an hour, three times a pump, because the mains is the fattest source in the game. Lower it if filling your whole reserve before the shutoff feels too easy.
Sandbox_WaterPipes_WaterStagnation_toolt: When on, water left sitting in a container or pipe network turns tainted after a while, and rain contaminates any open water left outside. Drawing from a network, refilling it, or town water flowing through it all count as movement and keep it fresh. Turn off to keep stored water clean forever.
Sandbox_WaterPipes_StagnationDaysClosed: Days before sealed water goes bad
Sandbox_WaterPipes_StagnationDaysClosed_: How many days a sealed container (a covered tank, the pipe network itself, a lidded amphora) may sit with no movement before its water turns tainted. Sealed water keeps for weeks, so this is the long timer. Set to 0 so sealed water never goes bad.
Sandbox_WaterPipes_StagnationDaysOpen: Days before open water goes bad
Sandbox_WaterPipes_StagnationDaysOpen_to: How many days an open, rain-catching container (a rain barrel, an uncovered amphora) may sit with no movement before its water turns tainted. Open water spoils in days, so this is the short timer. Set to 0 so open water never goes bad on its own (rain can still taint it).
Sandbox_WaterPipes_RainTaintsOpenWater_t: When on, rain falling on an open container left outside taints its whole network, so uncovered collection is a gamble whenever the weather turns. Turn off if you would rather open containers only spoil from sitting still.
Sandbox_WaterPipes_HydrantReserve_toolti: How much water a fire hydrant still holds in its local main once the town water is cut. 1000 by default. While the water service is on the hydrant is mains-fed and effectively bottomless; this is only what is left afterwards, and it drains as you use it. Set to 0 so hydrants run dry the moment the water stops.
Sandbox_WaterPipes_HydrantHead_tooltip: Pressure an open, mains-fed fire hydrant holds its network at, in tenths of a metre of water column. 400 = 40.0, well above the household mains (25.0) and a sprinkler's 20.0, because a hydrant is a high-flow tap on the town main. Opening one runs sprinklers far from any barrel with no pump, right up to the day the water is cut, after which the hydrant still yields its reserve but with no pressure. Lower it to make hydrants less of a free pump.
